title: The orange you picked also recolours lava, quench crust and warm water — check these
question: You chose the orange for fire. It is the same two constants that colour these. Do lava, the quench crust and a warm pan still look right to you, or did I break something you had already judged?
context_md:
This is the due-diligence half of the fire-colour card. / are not fire's alone — every cell above ambient blends toward them, so **lava, fresh quench crust and warm water all move with fire.** I said on that card that someone would have to re-check these three before it lands; this is that check, and you are the one who judged them originally.

**My own reading, for what it is worth — and please overrule it:** lava reads *better*, not worse. The falling blob went from a pale sandy cream to a saturated orange, which looks more like molten rock and less like sand, and the quench crust at the waterline reads more clearly as hot. I could not get warm water to show a difference at all: by the time the pan is worth photographing it has cooled, and at the frames where it is hot the tint barely registers against the blue.

**A is the old pair** ( 180,55,20 /  255,210,110). **B is what you chose** ( 150,30,12 /  255,138,36). Not blinded — you have already made the fire call and this is only about the collateral.

If any of these is worse, the fix is cheap: I can give fire its own tint pair rather than sharing one, at the cost of a second pair of constants.
